channel.title: Arch Linux: Recent news updates
channel.description: The latest and greatest news from the Arch Linux distribution.

item.title: Update to php ≥ 8.5.12 and/or php-legacy ≥ 8.3.36 to prevent remote code execution
item.description:
PHP versions prior to 8.5.12 and 8.3.36 are affected by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which allow for remote code execution.

For any system publicly exposing a PHP application with the help of a prior version of PHP, we urge users to upgrade those systems to the latest available version of PHP (php ≥ 8.5.12 and php-legacy ≥ 8.3.36) immediately.

Edit: For further details and instructions, please refer to the Arch Linux Security Advisories ASA-202610-1 and ASA-202610-2.
item.dc:creator: David Runge

item.title: Update to ca-certificates-mozilla ≥ 3.131.1-1 to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks
item.description:
On 2026-10-20 it was revealed, that several certificates of the eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authority have been compromised.

The compromised certificates have been removed/invalidated with ca-certificates-mozilla ≥ 3.131.1-1.

Without an update to this central certificate bundle, systems are susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks. As such, we urge everyone to upgrade their systems immediately.
item.dc:creator: David Runge

item.title: Mkinitcpio >=42 requires manual intervention for TPM2-based unlocking of LUKS devices
item.description:
Starting with package version 42-1, the mkinitcpio systemd hook now includes systemd-pcrosseparator.service (as intended by systemd v261).

This affects the measurements of PCR values 0-7, 9 and 12-14. If you configured the systemd hook and unlock LUKS partitions, that depend on these values, you need to re-enroll the TPM2 in use.

For guidance, please refer to systemd-cryptenroll(1), or the ArchWiki article on systemd-cryptenroll, when using pinned values. Refer to systemd-pcrlock(8), when relying on custom policies and a disabled systemd-pcrlock-make-policy.service.
item.dc:creator: David Runge
